_notes: This file is the source of truth for the reading list.
Run scripts/generate.py to render reading-list/README.md from this JSON.
Each entry has a dated_through field — items past their dated_through are pruned automatically.
Add new entries with the current date as added_on.
Per Ch 49: read one substantive piece per week, discuss one piece per month with the platform team, write one short note per quarter on what changed.

primary_sources.name: Anthropic engineering blog
primary_sources.why: Closest thing to ground truth on Claude's behavior, capabilities, and best-practice prompt patterns. Short, dense, no fluff.
primary_sources._review_note: Re-verify URL annually; vendor blog organization changes.

primary_sources.name: Anthropic Claude release notes
primary_sources.why: What changed in the model and API. Read every release.

primary_sources.name: OpenAI changelog
primary_sources.why: Even if you're not building on OpenAI, you should know what they shipped.

primary_sources.name: Google DeepMind / Gemini release notes
primary_sources.why: Gemini's coding capability has been moving fast in 2025-2026. Track for benchmark and price-point shifts.

primary_sources.name: Cursor changelog
primary_sources.why: If your team uses Cursor (most do), the changelog tells you when capabilities changed materially.

primary_sources.name: GitHub Copilot announcements
primary_sources.why: Copilot is the inline-completion default at most companies; track Microsoft's pace.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: METR evaluations
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: The 2025 RCT on AI productivity in real codebases, plus the 2026 follow-up, are the strongest empirical evidence on what AI tooling actually does to engineering throughput. Required reading for any leader making the AI rollout case.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: DORA — State of DevOps Report
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Annual. Now includes AI-tooling correlations with the four DORA metrics. The empirical baseline for 'is this working at scale?'

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: DX quarterly impact reports
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Largest credible empirical dataset on developer productivity (~135K developers tracked). Their AI-specific cuts are valuable.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: GitClear — code shape reports
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Published evidence on the long-term effects of AI coding assistance on code quality. Uncomfortable findings worth engaging with honestly.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: Faros AI — enterprise telemetry
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Telemetry-driven view of AI tooling adoption and outcomes at the enterprise tier. Useful for benchmark-against-others.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: Sonar — annual State of Code Quality
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Code-quality trend data. Relevant to any conversation about whether AI tooling is making code worse or better.

research_papers_and_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified leaderboard
research_papers_and_benchmarks.why: Public benchmark for agentic coding capability. Useful directionally; not a substitute for your internal benchmark (see benchmarks/ in this repo).

practitioner_writing.name: Sean Goedecke
practitioner_writing.why: Consistently sharp on the craft of working with agents — the seven slop signatures, code review intuition. The book quotes him.

practitioner_writing.name: Birgitta Böckeler
practitioner_writing.why: Her ongoing 'Exploring Generative AI' memo on Martin Fowler's site is one of the most patient, hands-on practitioner views.

practitioner_writing.name: Simon Willison
practitioner_writing.why: Daily-updated public lab notebook on what's new in AI tooling. The 'datasette' and 'llm' projects are themselves worth studying.

practitioner_writing.name: Andrej Karpathy
practitioner_writing.why: Deeper-than-most explanations of what's actually happening inside the models. Read the writing, also watch the videos.

practitioner_writing.name: Jesse Vincent
practitioner_writing.why: Practical writing on building with agents from someone deeply in the work.

practitioner_writing.name: Hamel Husain
practitioner_writing.why: Strong on evaluations, fine-tuning, and the operational side of running models in production.

practitioner_writing.name: Eugene Yan
practitioner_writing.why: Patterns for ML and LLM systems. The 'Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products' essay is foundational.

practitioner_writing.name: Latent Space (Swyx and Alessio)
practitioner_writing.why: Podcast and newsletter. Strong on the founder/builder perspective; useful for understanding the vendor side of the market.

practitioner_writing.name: The Pragmatic Engineer (Gergely Orosz)
practitioner_writing.why: Engineering management and culture writing. AI-tooling-specific posts have been particularly grounded.

podcasts.name: How About Tomorrow?
podcasts.why: Deep dives into what's emerging in software engineering with AI. Adam Elmore, Dax Raad and friends.

podcasts.name: Lenny's Podcast
podcasts.why: Product-management-focused but with frequent AI-tooling guests; useful for the cross-functional view.

_retired._note: Items removed from the active list. Kept here for the maintainer's reference, NOT included in the rendered README. When an item is retired, copy the entry here with a 'retired_on' date and brief 'retired_because' note.
